QB Notes: How well did things go for Patrick Mahomes in Josh Downs’ Chiefs debut? He scored the sixth most fantasy points of his illustrious career. It came as Downs played only 10 snaps, so in some ways, it is difficult to read too much into it. In others, however, it confirms that the Chiefs’ post-deadline change in attitude could be just as important as their change in personnel. They want to be the Chiefs again. Horrid Arizona will give them the opportunity to do so in Week 11. … When last we left Caleb Williams he was having by far his worst start under Ben Johnson. More specifically, by far his worst half. We hope some kind of “blueprint” was not laid down for the rest of the league to follow, but thankfully very few teams have the personnel to copy the Bucs' Vikings-esque approach. It certainly is not going to be an option for the Saints’ undermanned defense. … Jayden Daniels is actually outside the top 12 by average fantasy points, but there is little chance that holds for another readymade Bengals shootout. CIN/WAS is tied for the week’s highest over/under at 54.5.

C.J. Stroud is all the way up to QB4 overall status by average weekly points. That was hard to see coming during his disastrous postseason run. Houston's woeful run game and struggling defense mean Stroud's pass-first ways should continue, though his Week 11 ceiling might be capped by the Texans being nearly two-touchdown home favorites vs. the hollowed-out Colts. … Brock Purdy is blowing the doors off the 2026 season. Now he has his toughest test in the Vikings’ pass-erasing defense. Unlike some teams, the 49ers have the ground game to counteract the Vikes’ blitzes, while they also have the league’s pre-eminent misdirection maestro in Kyle Shanahan. This will not be Purdy’s most productive start of the year, but he feels like an exception to the “no quarterback finishes inside the top 12 against Minnesota” rule. … We thought Kirk Cousins was inheriting a deeper skill corps when he made the move from Las Vegas to Minnesota, but Jordan Addison (thumb) is on injured reserve while T.J. Hockenson (wrist, chest) remains on the injury report. Cousins at least still has his Bowers-ian figure in Justin Jefferson. Most Vikings game environments will be dominated by defense, but Week 11 in San Francisco will probably be an exception. Cousins cracks the top 12 in game two for Minnesota.

Tyler Shough has provided more than one score just one time in his past six starts. That distinct lack of upside makes it almost impossible to crack the top 12 even with six teams on bye, but the Saints’ complete lack of rushing threat coupled with Jordyn Tyson’s fast NFL start means his arm will be option A, B and C in a game where the Saints are two-score road underdogs. Everyone’s favorite 27-year-old sophomore could flirt with 50 attempts in the Windy City. … Cam Ward is suddenly playing the best football of his career even with Carnell Tate (shoulder) on the shelf. Now the Titans are “hoping” Tate returns after a two-game absence, while Wan’Dale Robinson will miss at least four weeks after landing on injured reserve with an ankle issue. Although it feels a bit point chasey, Week 11 is setting up as the perfect Ward streamer storm, as six teams are on bye and his defensive matchup could scarcely be more appealing in the Cowboys. Ward can’t crack the top 20, but for the first time this season, he is finally in the top 20.

Mistakes were made by J.J. McCarthy in Week 10, none worse than his game-losing interception late in the fourth quarter. He also made a bunch of stick ‘em throws beforehand, while his overall play has been much cleaner than it was in Minnesota. The Jags are a tough defensive test, but McCarthy’s willingness to go big-play hunting with both his arm and legs makes him an ideal bye week fill-in with 18.75 percent of the league sitting Week 11 out. … Aaron Rodgers bookended the Steelers’ Week 9 bye with two of his worst starts of the season. Although receiver reinforcements appear to be on the way in Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot), “enough people to throw to” hasn’t really been Rodgers’ 2026 issue. He just doesn’t have that compelling of a floor, while his spiked week potential is highly limited. … Jacoby Brissett threw 49 passes in his Ravens debut, which is six more than Lamar Jackson has ever attempted. Translation, this is a much different offense with Brissett under center, one that is more fantasy friendly for a broader set of skill players because of Brissett’s “attempts are a quarterback stat” nature. Brissett will still struggle to create fantasy value of his own, but byemageddon coupled with Baltimore’s status as a road underdog (read: lots of throws) has Brissett safely ensconced in the top 20.

Justin Herbert attempted a season-low 18 passes against the Ravens while dialing up a season-high seven rushes. Now, against all odds, the Bolts are actually favored for Week 11 against the Jets. Expect a similar offensive approach, with the Chargers leaning on the run and trying to limit Herbert’s sack and turnover opportunities. That is not a solid streamer strategy, but it should at least ensure a non-embarrassing floor. … Quarterback desperados are going to have to do some weird things with six teams on bye. Starting Joe Milton will most definitely be one of them. Hopefully getting both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) back following the Eagles’ bye week, Milton could actually have the passers to add a “dual” to this threat, which was decidedly mono via his legs in Week 9. … Fernando Mendoza took a billion sacks in his starting debut and lost his only difference-making pass catcher in Brock Bowers to an ankle injury. Even were Bowers to suit up and limp around against the Broncos’ elite pass defense, Mendoza isn’t in a position to crack the top 20 at the moment.

item.title: Should Packers fans hold onto hope for Trey Smack?
item.description: History suggests struggling young kickers can turn things around. But Green Bay is running out of time to find out.
item.content:encoded:
The Green Bay Packers have a Smack problem. Er, let me rephrase that. Rookie kicker Trey Smack has fallen far short of expectations in his first 10 games for the Packers. There, that’s better. 

Through those 10 games, he’s converted just 71.4% of his field-goal attempts and missed three extra points. Those numbers simply aren’t good enough. Not to win the Super Bowl. Not to win the division. Not to win 10 total games. 

But should we kick our Smack habit already? Sorry, I couldn’t resist. Anyway, it seems like there’s some decent historical evidence in favor of sticking with him. For now.

Younghoe Koo is an interesting comparison. After making just three of six field goal attempts during his brief rookie stint with the Chargers in 2017, Koo was released. He eventually worked his way back into the NFL and became, on balance, a very reliable NFL kicker. His current career field goal percentage sits at 85.3% and he’s made 95.9% of extra point attempts. 

But you don’t even need to leave Brown County. Mason Crosby hit a bump in the road in 2012, making just 63.6% of his field goal attempts. The team stuck with him. Not apples to apples, because that was his 6th season with the team. Even still, he kicked for eleven more seasons after that, wrapping up his career at an 81.3% make clip. 

Look. I’m not naive. Neither of these examples guarantees Smack will figure things out. But they demonstrate that periods of struggle don’t necessarily define a kicker’s career.

It’s also worth noting that Smack has legitimate credentials. At Florida, he converted 82.8% of his field-goal attempts and made 10 of 13 from beyond 50 yards. There’s something there.

Still, there’s a difference between developing a young kicker and repeatedly excusing poor performance. The Packers have already experienced the consequences of getting it wrong with Anders Carlson and Brayden Narveson (fights off flashbacks).

Smack deserves an opportunity to respond, but fans deserve an opportunity to comfortably take a bathroom break during an extra point attempt. He shouldn’t be handed the job indefinitely. He needs to gain consistency rather urgently. He doesn’t need to be perfect from here on out, but if he doesn’t improve, that doesn’t bode well for his roster spot.
